title: How "Pilarena" and "Congo Mulence" were written
summary: He wrote "Pilarena" at the Palladium after a girl from Pinar del Rio; Nilo Curbelo wrote it out and Puente arranged it for Pupi Campo.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Ah-Ha. What are some of the other tunes that you've written, Macho?
Well, 'La Paella'. That was Federico that asked me if I ever tried Paella, you know, the Spanish dish. I said: Oh, come on Federico, I even know how to make it.
And then you ran out and you wrote a tune.
Absolutely.
And you wrote 'Pilarena' ....
"Pilarena"
... with Tito Puente?
Well, this is a long story. I wrote the number. In those days ....
But, wait a minute, "Pilarena" was first recorded by Pupi Campo in 1948 or '49. So that means that it must have been written back then.
Yes, I wrote it at the Palladium.
Tell me about that. How did that come about?

Well, ahh - there was a girl that she said she came from Pinar del Rio, so pinar, pinar, Pinar del Rio. Pinar was - they had pines - there's a lot of pine trees in Pinar del Rio, so they call it "Pilarena", pi, Pilarena. So we was talking, you know, and I just listen to the girl. She says she is from Pinar del Rio. I say: Yeah, I am going to write a rumba. I didn't even say I am going to write a rumba. I just got in to the table because my band
was rehearsing and I start to write "Pinarena", and with melody and lyrics, and Curbelo's nephew that he used to play trumpet with ....
Nilo?

.. Nilo, Nilo Curbelo. In those days, as always, it's kind of difficult to write a Cuban music. The phrasing es very difficult, but Curbelo being Cuban and trumpet player so he had a more better idea to write the number than Tito Puente. Tito Puente was young, he haven't got that experience to write a real Cuban number, so Curbelo wrote the number and then I give it to Tito to make me an arrangement.
I see.
So he made an arrangement and I played once or twice and he made another arrangement for Pupi Campo and Pupi Campo recorded it first. I never recorded it.
You never recorded it.
Never recorded it.
Tito never recorded it either, right?
No, I don't think so.
I have the Pupi Campo arrangement, I have the recording and it's very, very good.
Yeah.
So that's how it came about.
And I wrote another number too, that I, what you call it, the, the ....
"Congo Mulence"?
"Congo Mulence"
Is in one of Tito Puente's album.
Uh - huh.
